newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm as three new issues emerged to take advantage of an ongoing rally.

-- Swedish mortgage bank Spintab issued a 125 million Swiss franc bond maturing January 2002 with a 3.25 pct coupon priced at 102.70 via CSFB. It was quoted by the lead yielding 3.03 percent in late trade.

-- Oppland Energiverke also set a 150 million franc issue, maturing May 2003 with a 3.50 percent coupon priced at 102.00, via CSFB. The issuer is a Norwegian power producer, and the issue is backed by the state of Oppland. The issue was quoted yielding 3.48 percent.
-- Oesterreichische Kontrollbank set a 250 mllion franc offering for four years, maturing March 2001, with a 2.75 percent coupon priced at 102.00 via Bank von Ernst.
It was quoted by the lead at 2.63 percent.
One trader said there was good demand for medium maturities. But traders said there was little demand in the market generally.

"Cash was totally quiet, in futures it was totally quiet. At the moment the market is rising, and as market maker, if a customer buys something, you have to cover," one Swiss-based trader at a major Swiss bank said.
The Swiss bond market has staged a more or less continued rise since July. The March Confederate bond futures contract has also made progressively new gains, hitting a fresh high of 118.10 on Monday.
March Comi medium-term bond up 12 at 111.30
Mar Euro Swiss francs up three at 98.29.
